thread:
alex chen: hey — first week setup question. I need Parallels + Windows for a client repro but my M1 MBP (company-provisioned) is blocking the install. Parallels crashes during kernel extension load and the installer shows a 'permission denied' modal. Anyone seen this with Kandji profiles?

alex chen: error popup text: "Parallels Desktop cannot be installed because system policy prevents loading the kernel extension. Contact your administrator."

alex chen: also tried toggling reduced security in Recovery (did the csrutil check) but I'm not allowed to change settings — the option is greyed out. FileVault is on.

alex chen: @dylan-it any chance I can get temporary admin to complete the installer, or is there an approved workflow?

dylan-it: hey alex — welcome! we usually avoid granting full admin for installs like this. two options: 1) we push an approved Parallels package via the MDM, or 2) we schedule a quick remote session and we escalate just for the install.

dylan-it: can you share `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep Serial` and the exact macOS build? (apple menu -> About this Mac -> Version)

alex chen: serial: C02ABC12345G
macOS: Ventura 13.5.2 (22G90)

tara it: tagging for MDM policy review — some legacy profiles block third-party kexts and virtualization flags. @it-bot can you check if this device has the "restrict-kext" config enabled in kandji?

it-bot: [automated] Device C02ABC12345G — profile scan:
- enrolled: yes
- FileVault: enabled
- restrictions: com.redwood.restrict-kext = true
- admin rights: standard user (no sudo)

sean eng: fwiw Parallels has an M1/arm support shim but it still needs the kernel extensions or user-allowed system extensions on older Ventura builds. We moved devs to a containerized Windows image but I know some folks need full Parallels.

dylan-it: ok — shortest path: i'll schedule a 20m remote session and temporarily push a narrower policy that allows the parallels-kext certificate. no full admin. alex do you have a good window today?

alex chen: yes, 3:30-4:00pm PT works. thanks.

dylan-it: scheduled 15m: join link sent via DM. steps during session:
1) we create a temporary MDM patch: allow-kext-parallels (scoped to your serial).
2) we trigger the Parallels installer under an escalated ephemeral process so kext can load.
3) verify Parallels VM boots and Windows activates.
4) revert MDM patch so policy returns to default.

alex chen: appreciated. quick Q: will this touch the FileVault key or escrow? i have a personal recovery key message that popped earlier during enroll.

dylan-it: no changes to FileVault keys. we won't touch escrow or keychain. just toggling kext allowlist for the certificate ID.

tara it: note for ops: after the session, we should add a KB note for new-hires who need Parallels — avoid repetitive manual escalations. include the exact cert SHA and MDM patch name.

alex chen: joined the session, installer ran, got one more prompt to "approve system extension" in Security & Privacy — clicked allow, rebooted. Parallels now starts and I can create a Win11 ARM VM. all good on my end. :party_parrot:

dylan-it: thanks — confirmed device C02ABC12345G shows allowed cert SHA 9f:3b:4a:... in kandji and policy reverted. closing the temporary patch.

it-bot: [automated] Action log: temporary-policy allow-kext-parallels applied -> removed. Timestamp 2101235600.

alex chen: leaving a quick note here: if you need Parallels on company M1/M2 machines, file a request in #new-hires and mention the serial, macOS build, and whether FileVault is on. Saves time.

sean eng: nice — thanks for the writeup alex. saved me a support ping later.

alex chen: thanks everyone!
